title: Full faithfulness of closed direct image
statement:
For any closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$, the adjunction counit
$i^*i_*G\to G$ is an isomorphism on all pro-etale module sheaves over a
finite constant ring. Thus $i_*$ is fully faithful, without a
constructibility hypothesis.

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-closed-site-adjunction] on the affine pro-etale sites over A and A/I. It gives v left adjoint to u with invertible unit. Opposites followed by precomposition with functors to ModuleCat R give an adjunction whose right adjoint is precomposition with u.op and whose counit is the image of the original unit, hence invertible. Thus precomposition with u.op is fully faithful. Restriction from the full pro-etale site to its affine basis is an equivalence on sheaves. The direct-image restriction square commutes definitionally, so closed direct image along Spec(A/I) -> Spec A is fully faithful on sheaves too. Therefore its upper-star/lower-star counit is invertible. This works for any coefficient ring R, in particular the finite constant ring of the node.

A closed immersion into an affine scheme factors, up to source and target scheme isomorphisms, as a quotient-spectrum immersion. Pushforward along a scheme isomorphism is an equivalence. Transport full faithfulness through lowerStarComp and lowerStarCongr to obtain the counit isomorphism whenever the target is affine.

Choose an affine open cover of the arbitrary target and pull it back to the source. By [lem-exc-closed-localization], the lower-star square has invertible weakly-etale base-change mate. Taking a second mate gives the conjugate of the original square isomorphism and is therefore invertible. The mate-counit identity then identifies the restriction of the global counit with an invertible affine counit, up to these isomorphisms. Restrictions along the pulled-back Zariski open cover jointly detect isomorphisms. Hence the original counit is invertible, and closed direct image is fully faithful.

proof_origin.place: Tags 09BK and 097P; closed-site adjunction followed by Mathlib adjunctions on opposites, precomposition, iterated mates, and open-cover conservativity.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $R$ be a ring and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ any closed immersion. On
pro-etale sheaves of $R$-modules the adjunction counit $i^*i_*G\to G$ is an
isomorphism for every $G$. Thus $i_*$ is fully faithful, without a
constructibility hypothesis.

proof.text:
First let $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. On the
affine ind-etale bases, base change $u$ to $Z$ is right adjoint to the
closed-site lift $v$ with invertible unit $\operatorname{id}\to uv$
([lem-exc-closed-site-adjunction]). Passing to opposite categories and
precomposing, precomposition with $u$ is therefore fully faithful on
presheaves of $R$-modules: its adjoint has an invertible counit, given at a
presheaf $F$ by $F$ applied to the unit of $v\dashv u$. Restriction of sheaves
to these bases is an equivalence, and on the bases the direct image $i_*$ is
precomposition with $u$, so $i_*$ is fully faithful. An arbitrary closed
immersion into an affine scheme is isomorphic to such a quotient immersion,
and direct images compose, so $i_*$ is fully faithful whenever $X$ is affine;
equivalently the counit is an isomorphism.

In general, cover $X$ by affine opens $X_k$ and put $Z_k=Z\times_XX_k$. The
restrictions to the $Z_k$ form a pro-etale cover of $Z$, so a map of sheaves on
$Z$ is an isomorphism once its restrictions to all $Z_k$ are. By
[lem-exc-closed-localization], applied to the cartesian squares formed by the
open immersions $X_k\to X$, $Z_k\to Z$ and the closed immersions, restriction
to $Z_k$ carries the counit of $i^*\dashv i_*$ to the counit for
$Z_k\hookrightarrow X_k$, up to isomorphism. These affine counits are
isomorphisms by the first step, so the global counit is an isomorphism. An
adjunction has fully faithful right adjoint precisely when its counit is an
isomorphism, giving the assertion.
